en_summary: Asian neoclouds deals with Bytedance/Tencent cancelled due to US export controls, rerouting spare capacity to US players; $CRWV cited 10x demand > supply into 2027 so no compute flooding crash expected. Financing cancellations mean less future competition, good for $NBIS long-term as well-capitalized neoclouds with hyperscaler counterparties win; macro risks like rates impact neoclouds most.
text:
Of course! uhh two things: 

1. Asian neoclouds (eg. Malaysia/Thailand) had their deals cancelled with Bytedance, Tencent etc. due to US export controls. 

So they'll reroute spare capacity back to US players. 

Many are arguing that creates compute flooding, but $CRWV cited 10x demand > supply entering 2027. 

So even if supply comes in, I would still see a large demand imbalance, not prices crashing. If anything... pricing has still gone up from some trackers. But we'll see the full effects in the incoming weeks. 

2. Asian Neoclouds had their financing cancelled/paused due to ongoing risks. 

This is more nuanced, it means less compute/competition comes online in the future, which is a good thing for players like $NBIS? 

It might hurt some semi supply chains (not US neoclouds) as seen with some spot prices dropping around GPU/DRAM  procurement. 

But China would need to build out their own compute anyway for their frontier labs so I see a primarily shift in order timing + bifurcated supply chains than aggregate demand falling. 

I see the well capitalized Neoclouds (with hyperscaler counterparties) winning in the long run like $NBIS, but as Elon said with the "other gupplies" there might be some trouble. 

There's still the overall macro risks like rate hikes, financing, etc. where Neoclouds are typically the most impacted

Too many multifaceted variables at play here; but I think Weebius is the best and ends up on top

DOES A $VIX SPIKE MEAN BUY? THE ACADEMIC EVIDENCE, THE REBUTTALS, AND A CONCLUSION

THE CLAIM

The folk version says buy when the fear gauge screams. The academic version is narrower and more interesting: expected equity returns step up, nonlinearly, after implied volatility reaches extreme levels, and the step-up is large enough to measure years of data at a time. Both versions circulate every time the VIX prints 30 or 35. They are not the same claim, and the literature supports them very differently.

• Ronn and Xu (Econometrics, 2025) test the folk version directly. Across 29 historical episodes in which the VIX exceeded 30, a strategy of cutting equity exposure above 30 and buying back when volatility subsided underperformed simply holding through the episodes by 10.9% a year. Subsequent S&P 500 returns rose with the level of the VIX. Their conclusion for investors with a high appetite for risk: when the VIX is high, invest, because on average you will be compensated.

Holtz-Eakin is reading the wrong gauge, and the Fed shouldn’t follow him.

Nominal GDP is not a measure of overheating. It counts output and prices together. Third-quarter nominal growth was 6.2%, and 4.3 points of that was real output . Prices contributed about 1.9 points, which is target-consistent. Calling that “excessively demand-driven” misreads the arithmetic.

His argument also has no place for productivity. With GDP revised up, Q3 productivity is heading from 3.6% to 4.8% annualised. Hours barely moved, so the output is coming from each worker producing more. Unit labour costs were already falling, and that revision pushes them lower. Overheated demand does the opposite.

“Core inflation has never come close to 2%” is no case for a 50 basis point hike. The energy shock that has inflated prices will dissipate by spring, when the base effects roll off and PCE returns toward 2%. A hike cannot produce a barrel of oil. It would tighten against a price shock that is already ending, and a Fed that hikes to “send a message” is substituting posture for policy.

The cost of that message is large. A 50 basis point move would put the real funds rate above neutral and tighter than Greenspan’s in 1995, just as the productivity gains he bet on appear in the data. A Fed that cannot tell a supply boom from a demand boom should not set rates.

Ran Neuner says AI agents will turn your $10,000 deposit into 1,000 transactions chasing yield, and bank rails aren't built for that

"When you go to a bank and you park money for a year, you go to the bank and you say, hey, here's $10,000. And the reason why that's one transaction is because humans don't like friction."

"They aggregate things into packages, right? Like you can lock money up for a year or 6 months or 9 months or 30 days."

"What an AI agent will do, it'll take the same $10,000, it'll lock it up for 3 hours in one vault, 6 hours in another vault, 12 hours in another vault, 14 hours in another vault, and it'll keep jumping around from vault to vault to optimize your return."

"Couple things are going to happen. One, you're going to get a much better return than if you just locked it up for a year because the agent is optimizing."

"The second thing is that the agent's going to be a thousand transactions where typically as a human you would have done one transaction."

"My thesis has always been that they're going to allocate on blockchain. Now everywhere I go, even BlackRock wrote a report that basically said ACH rails are no good for this. It's some kind of blockchain."

text: The chip selling on yesterday had a specific cause, and it was not the tariff headline. The Commerce Department's November 16 rule closed the loophole that let Chinese firms rent Nvidia chips remotely through overseas data centers, and it took effect Nov 19. On Wednesday the consequence arrived in the open: sellers dumping Blackwell B300 GPUs on the secondary market, with servers quoted at $3M against a $600k list price, because the chips can no longer be rented to the customers they were bought for. TSMC has suspended previously permitted advanced chip orders from Chinese customers. The rule is aimed at the cloud loophole, and it works by cutting the rental route, not just the shipping route. For $NVDA the read is mixed: the demand is real, the chips are real, but a slice of that demand was Chinese money routed through Southeast Asia, and that slice is now stranded. The market is repricing which AI demand is durable and which was regulatory arbitrage.

text: The fear gauge told yesterday 's story better than the index did. The VIX spiked toward 35 in the morning as the tape flushed, then faded to around 28 by the close. Fear peaked while prices were at their lows, and fear faded while prices recovered. That is the normal shape of a capitulation day, not a market breaking down. The protection trade grew into the close though, with the $VIX still up on the day even as stocks bounced, which says hedgers were buying the rally rather than chasing it. The level to watch is 30. Above it, fear is in charge. Below it, the market is healing. Wednesday closed under it after spending the morning above it, and gold and bonds both gained on the day, which is the protection trade staying on. Tuesday's close was 26.36, so 28 is still elevated, just no longer panicked. Friday's thin session will tell us whether the fade continues or the fear comes back. A quiet Friday says the worst is over. A VIX back above 30 says it is not.

text:
The Nasdaq-100 is cheaper on forward earnings today than it was at the bottom of the dot-com crash.

Its forward P/E is  17x right now, the lowest in four years. At the October 2002 bottom, after the index had fallen 83%, the forward P/E was still 20-25x. The index stands 32 times higher than that bottom and cheaper on earnings.

The 2002 number needs its context. That ~20-25x sat on earnings that had collapsed, so it was never actually cheap. Today's ~17x sits on earnings that are real and still growing. Same multiple math, opposite setup.

The tech premium has vanished too. The Nasdaq-100 now trades at roughly the same forward multiple as the S&P 500. Cheap does not mean the selling is over, the tape still has to confirm the turn. But the valuation case for the Nasdaq has not been this strong since the last time it bottomed.
